speaker: Operator
text: Welcome to Walmart's second quarter fiscal '27 earnings call.

speaker: Operator
text: At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode.

speaker: Operator
text: If anyone should require operator assistance during the conference, please press star-0 on your telephone keypad.

text: I'll now turn the conference over to Steph Wissing, Senior Vice President, Investor Relations.

speaker: Senior Vice President, Investor Relations · Steph Wissing
text: Welcome, everyone.

speaker: Senior Vice President, Investor Relations · Steph Wissing
text: Joining me today from our home office in Bentonville are CEO John Furner and CFO John David Rainey.

speaker: Senior Vice President, Investor Relations · Steph Wissing
text: We'll begin with highlights of the previous quarter and our outlook for the year.

speaker: Senior Vice President, Investor Relations · Steph Wissing
text: Then we'll open the line for your questions.

speaker: Senior Vice President, Investor Relations · Steph Wissing
text: During the question-and-answer portion, we've invited Seth Delaire, our Chief Growth Officer, as well as segment leadership to join: Dave Gugina from Walmart U.S., Chris Nicholas from Walmart International, and Latrice Watkins from Sam's Club U.S., so we can address as many of your questions as possible.

speaker: Senior Vice President, Investor Relations · Steph Wissing
text: Please limit yourself to one question.

speaker: Senior Vice President, Investor Relations · Steph Wissing
text: For additional detail on our results, including highlights by segment, please see our earnings release and supplemental presentation on our website.

speaker: Senior Vice President, Investor Relations · Steph Wissing

speaker: Senior Vice President, Investor Relations · Steph Wissing
text: That concludes my introduction.

speaker: Senior Vice President, Investor Relations · Steph Wissing
text: John, over to you.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: Good morning and thanks for joining us.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: I want to start by thanking our associates around the world.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: Their commitment to serving customers and members every day is what drives our business, and the results we delivered this quarter reflect their hard work.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: This was a good quarter for Walmart and shows once again that our strategy is proving out.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: We've been investing against it for years, and I'm even more bullish today as we see the pieces increasingly powering each other: a strong retail foundation alongside faster-growing businesses like Marketplace, advertising, and membership.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: The math isn't simply one plus one equals two.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: The value comes from how these businesses work together, with each one strengthening the others and expanding what the company can do as a whole.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: And as these businesses scale, they become a more meaningful part of our mix and they're changing the shape of our business.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: We're accelerating growth and improving the overall economics of the company.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: The model is working, and we're confident in its power to drive durable long-term growth and shareholder value.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: The underlying business continued to perform well in the quarter and was largely in line with our expectations, which assumed a slight moderation in sales growth from the first quarter.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: Overall, we continue to gain market share.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: We grew units and transactions, and membership fee revenue was at an all-time high on growth of 17%.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: We delivered another quarter of strong eCommerce growth, up 23% globally, including the 10th consecutive quarter of growth over 20% for Walmart U.S.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: And we also expanded the reach of platform businesses like Walmart+ and Marketplace to markets outside the United States, demonstrating how we're leveraging these for growth.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: And as we build and scale these capabilities across markets and begin to operate globally on the platforms we built during the last few years of transformation, we're seeing the same dynamic.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: These businesses work together, deepen our relationship with customers and members, and create additional opportunities for growth and stronger economics.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: Our core retail business had another strong quarter with sales growth at the top end of our guidance, up 5% in constant currency.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: Comp sales for Walmart U.S. were 2.6%, led by transactions, and Sam's Club U.S. delivered comps of 4.4%.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: International was up 7.9%, led by China and India.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: For Walmart U.S., I feel good about how the underlying business is performing.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: The team delivered strong sales growth in categories like toys, pantry, and fresh, and we continue to see growth from higher-income households.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: Changes in regulation around maximum fair pricing for certain drugs negatively impacted comp sales by 125 basis points.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: John David will share more about the makeup of the U.S. comp and talk through the additional color we provided in today's earnings presentation.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: Turning to profits, adjusted operating income grew 17.4% in constant currency.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: This includes the benefit from the receipt of tariff refunds in the quarter.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: And as we suggested on the last call, our intent was to deploy much of that back into price, and that's what we're doing.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: Importantly, our underlying profit growth was where we thought it would be.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: Excluding this benefit, because of our strong top- and bottom-line growth, we're raising our guidance for the year.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: Now let me take a moment to talk about specific drivers of our growth.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: First, everything we do starts with serving customers and members as an omnichannel retailer.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: Core to that is delivering value and maintaining price leadership.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: As we said coming out of Q1, customers tell us they're still feeling some pressure, but it's clear customers are looking for value and convenience, and they want things fast.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: And that's where Walmart shines.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: Having the best prices across a basket of goods helps us continue to build trust with our customers and members by helping them save money at a time when many households are carefully managing their budgets.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: The Walmart U.S. team delivered more than 11,000 rollbacks during the quarter, up from 7,200 rollbacks at the end of the first quarter, demonstrating our commitment to price investment.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: We're investing heavily in price because customers need us to and because we believe it drives market share gains over time.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: Our price gaps to conventional grocers here in the U.S. are strong and they continue to widen.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: The share gains we see from this channel have persisted alongside the drug and dollar formats.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: A second area I'd like to highlight is our ongoing strength in eCommerce.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: The sustained growth we've seen in eCommerce across the company over multiple years points to more than a digital success story.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: It's evidence that customers and members increasingly choose Walmart because they know we combine low prices across a broad assortment with speed and convenience.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: The mix of eCommerce for Walmart International is now 30% with strong growth again this quarter in China, India, and Canada.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: Growth in Q2 was 19%.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: Sam's Club U.S. grew eCommerce 26% with delivery from club up triple digits.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: Following the launch of our one-hour delivery back in April, Walmart U.S. delivered growth of 24%.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: Marketplace grew 52% and advertising was up 38%.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: We believe a factor in this growth is our ability to deliver with speed.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: Customers and members around the world are getting super-fast deliveries of baskets that include pharmacy, fresh, frozen, fashion, and general merchandise, often in under 30 minutes.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: Fast delivery in the U.S. grew 48% for the quarter.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: Speed matters, and we have a significant competitive advantage.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: Our physical footprint, fulfillment infrastructure, and local delivery capabilities allow us to move closer to customers while maintaining an attractive cost structure.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: We've now expanded sub-30-minute delivery into 38 markets here in the U.S., giving millions of additional customers access to faster fulfillment.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: And speed isn't simply a fulfillment metric; it's an acquisition strategy.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: Customers who use fast delivery shop with us more frequently.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: They deepen engagement with us, and they're more likely to become Walmart+ members.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: The advances we're making in speed of delivery create another reason for customers to choose Walmart for more shopping occasions.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: That's an important shift in how we think about growth.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: And as we become faster, we're not simply taking share within traditional retail categories.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: We're expanding the number of occasions where Walmart can serve customers, like food delivery.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: In the past, customers may have thought about Walmart primarily for groceries and general merchandise.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: Today we're expanding beyond that.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: Meal solutions, prepared food, partnerships like the one we announced with Subway, and faster fulfillment allow us to participate in a much broader share of everyday food spending.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: This is an exciting opportunity, and we're just getting started.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: The third area I'd like to highlight is our platform strategy.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: We're building capabilities that are increasingly scalable across markets.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: Marketplace, fulfillment services, membership, advertising, and other commerce solutions are strengthening our business and they're improving the economics of the company.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: This quarter, we expanded our U.S. marketplace platform capabilities into both Mexico and Canada, and we launched Walmart in Canada.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: Membership was also a highlight with double-digit growth for Walmart Plus and strong growth for Sam's Club in the U.S., China and Mexico.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: We also gave a boost to our advertising business with the acquisition of VIZIO.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: We believe VIZIO expands our ability to help advertisers of all sizes reach customers through self-service tools while measuring results against real shopping behavior.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: Combined with Walmart Connect and VIZIO, this further strengthens our platform and creates value for customers, sellers, suppliers and advertisers.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: These are important milestones because they demonstrate the value we're creating across the company.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: Rather than building entirely new capabilities market by market, we're increasingly able to build once, improve continuously and scale globally.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: That makes us faster, more efficient and allows customers in more markets to benefit from innovations developed anywhere across Walmart Inc.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: The fourth area is our supply chain.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: We've invested in automation, technology, fulfillment capacity and our physical network.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: And these investments are showing up in customer experience.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: They're allowing us to move inventory more efficiently, deliver faster, help with in-stock levels and support the growth of both our first-party and marketplace businesses.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: They also strengthen the economics of our omnichannel model.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: And as we improve density and utilization across our network, speed and profitability reinforce one another, and you can see how these advantages build on each other.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: When we invest in our supply chain, it helps us get more products to our customers and members faster.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: When they get items faster, they shop with us more frequently both online and in our stores.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: And as frequency increases, our suppliers and sellers want to be closer to the point of purchase.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: It's reinforcing.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: Finally, let me talk about how AI is helping make Walmart faster, more convenient and personalized.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: We continue to take a people-led, tech-powered approach.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: We're using AI to make our work easier and help our associates grow and be at their very best.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: We believe AI will improve nearly every part of our business by making shopping better and our associates' work easier.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: Sparky is a great example.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: The number of customers using Sparky is up 70% from last year, and the customers and members who use Sparky for shopping spend 40% more per order than others who don't.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: Someone recently shared with me that they asked Sparky for a weekly meal plan of healthy foods with high-protein options.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: Within a few seconds, Sparky shared recipes and meal kits with the ability to add all the ingredients they needed to their basket with one click.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: Sparky even recognized the ingredients they'd recently purchased both online and in-store, so they didn't buy something they already had.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: It's building trust.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: When you step back, what encourages me the most is how these areas are increasingly connected.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: This isn't about any single driver.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: It's about building a business where each advantage reinforces the next.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: With that, I'll close my comments where I began, and that's by thanking our associates.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: The progress we're making is possible because of the way they serve customers and members each and every day, the way they embrace new technology, and the way they continue to find better ways to operate.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: I'm excited about the momentum we have, confident in the strategy we're executing, and even more optimistic about the opportunities ahead.

speaker: CEO · John Furner
text: With that, I'll turn it over to John David to walk through the quarter in more detail.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: I'll echo John's sentiments.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: We're pleased with the way our business is performing, especially during the more recent operating environment that's been marked by some near-term macro crosswinds.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Our business model is only getting stronger and more durable, and this gives us confidence to raise our sales and operating income growth guidance for the year.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: With the tariff refunds, there are some idiosyncrasies to this quarter's results, so I'll provide a deeper view of the impacts and discuss how we're thinking about these factors looking into the second half of the year.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: First, I'll start with the financial and operational highlights.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Enterprise net sales growth in constant currency of 5% was at the top end of our guidance of 4% to 5%, driven by growth in e-commerce, Sam's Club and China.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: This quarter demonstrates the benefits of our diversified portfolio of businesses across channels, formats and markets.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Global e-commerce net sales grew 23%, continuing the strong momentum of the last several years.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Sam's Club U.S. and our International segment were both accretive to enterprise sales growth.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Sam's comps were driven by a 7% increase in transactions with solid growth in unit volumes.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: International constant currency sales increased nearly 8%, led by 9.7% growth in China.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Walmart U.S. net sales increased 3.5%, including a comp sales increase ex-fuel of 2.6%, slightly below our initial expectation due to lower Health and Wellness sales that were impacted by a larger headwind from maximum fair pricing.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: I'll talk more about this in a minute.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Enterprise adjusted operating income on a constant currency basis increased over 17% and adjusted EPS increased over 19%.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: This performance reflects the net benefit from the tariff refunds we received, partially offset by price investments in the quarter, as well as improved incremental margins in our digital business, with strength in high-margin Commerce Solutions.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Operating income growth included a net benefit of approximately 750 basis points related to tariff refunds received in Q2.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Setting aside this benefit, underlying operating income growth was at the top end of our 7% to 10% guidance.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Our outlook reflects the continued prioritization of the remaining tariff refunds into customer experience and price investments in the second half.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: For this reason, I encourage you to consider Q2 and Q3 performance together to assess the underlying growth of the business.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: I want to take a moment to further emphasize the positive progress we're making in our e-commerce businesses.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Digital is driving our growth, customer spend and market share gains across all operating segments.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: As we deploy these digital capabilities outside the U.S., it allows us to move with speed from an operational perspective.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: From a financial perspective, this allows us to grow at a lower marginal cost.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Walmart U.S. e-commerce grew 24% in Q2 with over 40% sales growth in store-fulfilled deliveries, 20% growth in average weekly customers and over 50% growth in marketplace sales.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: E-commerce growth was also strong at Sam's Club U.S., up 26%, and our International segment up 19%, led by China, India and Canada.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Sustained e-commerce momentum enables the growth of Commerce Solutions businesses—advertising, marketplace, Data Ventures and membership.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: I'll start with Global Advertising, which increased 38%, driven by another strong quarter from Walmart Connect in the U.S. and Flipkart Ads.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Walmart U.S. advertising, including VIZIO, also increased 38%, led by strength in Walmart Connect, which was up 43%.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: The momentum in marketplace and fulfillment services continued this quarter with U.S. net sales up 52%.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Nearly 50% of the marketplace business flowed through Walmart Fulfillment Services in Q2, an increase of nearly 400 basis points versus last year.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: We're benefiting from a broader marketplace assortment that includes more of the key brands that customers want.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Walmart Data Ventures continues to drive meaningful growth.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Users value the platform's enhanced decision intelligence capabilities, which uncover shared growth opportunities across Walmart's formats and markets.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: We announced today that we're extending the Scintilla platform to Sam's Club U.S. next year, addressing one of the top requests from our suppliers.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Rounding out our profit mix drivers, membership income grew nearly 17% globally.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Sam's Club U.S. membership increased nearly 6%.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: This was driven by steady growth in member counts and Plus penetration.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Sam's Club China hit new record highs in member counts and we saw strong relative performance in our Sam's format in Mexico.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: We're especially pleased with the continued strong double-digit growth in our U.S.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Walmart Plus program, resulting in the best first half of membership growth in its history.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: We're building what we believe can be the most essential membership program for consumers and excited for what's ahead.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: The thing that people sometimes overlook when reflecting on our membership program is the incrementality that we see on GMV.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Our members spend approximately four times more than non-members.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Turning to incremental margins, the profitability of our eCommerce business continues to improve.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Our Walmart U.S. eCommerce business achieved double-digit incremental margins for the first half of the year.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: This was driven by continued strong ad and membership revenue, further densification of our delivery network, growth in fee-based fast deliveries, which represented an all-time high of 37% of store-fulfilled deliveries in the quarter, and, lastly, the benefits of automation.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: 3,100 of our U.S. stores are now served with some level of automated freight, and we're processing over 50% of our eCommerce fulfillment volume through automated facilities.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Now I want to address a few areas in a little more detail.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: The first is the Walmart U.S. comp.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: To help understand the composition of our U.S. comp sales by merchandise category, we provided an additional disclosure in our supplemental slide deck, which is slide 14.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: The chart on that slide shows Walmart U.S. comps excluding the Health and Wellness category.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Over the last two and a half years, sales in our core categories have been extremely consistent, largely in the 3% to 4% range on a quarterly basis.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: For outlier periods such as last quarter, when looking at a two-year average, growth falls right into the middle of a similar 3% to 4% range.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: We expect core comps in a similar range in the second half.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: However, when looking at the Walmart U.S. total comps, including health and wellness, during each of FY25 and FY26, we realized 100 basis points of a tailwind from sales of GLP-1 branded drugs.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: In FY27, the benefit from GLP-1 is expected to be roughly half that amount as scrip count growth is more than offset by price mix headwinds.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: New in FY27, we cited a 100 basis points headwind to total comp sales from deflation and brand-to-generic transfers under the first year of maximum fair price regulation.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: In Q2, this negative impact was closer to 125 basis points, and we've updated our estimate for FY27 impact to be similar at 125 basis points.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Putting all this together, sales of core merchandise categories have been consistent, but at the total U.S. comp level we've had nearly a 200 basis point net swing in comp sales growth from the trailing two-year pace to this year, entirely tied to our health and wellness category.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: It's important to note that this unfavorable impact is to the top line only.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: We're pleased with the underlying performance and the profit contribution of our health and wellness business.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Next, I want to discuss in-store comps.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: They were down low single digits in Q2, consistent with a trend that began in late Q4 last year.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: This headwind is primarily driven by the negative impact from the health and wellness business, where the vast majority of the sales occur in store.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: The role of our stores has evolved as our model has changed. eCommerce sales now represent over 23% of our mix in Walmart U.S., which is double the level from just five years ago.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: The more omni we become, the more important our stores become.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Not less important—more important.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Between in-store shopping and digital fulfillment, we have more unit volumes transacted through our stores than ever before, as they are the last-mile fulfillment nodes for 80% of our eCommerce orders and 100% of our fast deliveries.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: As eCommerce profit margins continue to improve, we're becoming increasingly agnostic about channel dynamics while enabling customers to shop on their terms.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Next, I want to discuss the tariff refunds in a little more detail.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: As we shared with you in May, we were eligible for approximately $2.9 billion of tariff refunds, amounting to about half a percent of annual U.S. net sales.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: To date, we've received substantially all of these tariff refunds.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: As John mentioned, we've taken a disciplined approach to investing these funds back into customer experience and price leadership, prioritizing investment in grocery and general merchandise categories.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Looking forward, our Q3 guidance reflects the continued impact of pricing actions taken in Q2 alongside continued prioritization of tariff refunds in the price investment.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: We would encourage you to look at our operating income growth for Q2 and Q3 together to assess the underlying performance of the business.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Now I'll turn to SG&A.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: We leveraged wages in Q2 as we continue to improve productivity through increased usage of tech tools by associates in stores and streamlined inventory flow enabled by supply chain automation.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: More than offsetting these benefits were higher depreciation related to capex and increased self-insurance cost.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Inventory at quarter-end increased 6% in constant currency, slightly higher than total enterprise sales growth.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: The increase reflects cost inflation as well as higher inventory to support strategic initiatives in the U.S., including the optimization of inventory across fulfillment nodes.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Turning to guidance, we have increased confidence in the long-term value drivers of our business.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Our business is strong; eCommerce and related businesses offer compelling growth; and we are consistently generating strong incremental margins.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: We're raising our fiscal year sales guidance to 4% to 5% from 3.5% to 4.5% previously.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: There are four assumptions worth highlighting.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: The first is this upward revision reflects the pass-through of first half performance but also assumes slightly better second half sales versus our prior guide as price investments drive accelerated and sustained share gains.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Price investments are an immediate benefit to customers but build value over time for the business.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Second, we're incorporating a larger headwind from maximum fair pricing within the Walmart U.S. business.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Based on year-to-date experience, we now estimate the full-year headwind to Walmart U.S. comp sales will be closer to 125 basis points.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Next, we expect Sam's Club U.S. and International to be growth-accretive to the enterprise in both Q3 and Q4.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Walmart U.S. sales growth is expected to improve in Q3 as the investment in customer value translates into stronger sales.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: And lastly, the timing of Flipkart's Big Billion Days will impact the cadence of Q3 and Q4 sales growth this year.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: We expect a Q3 headwind of over 100 basis points to sales growth as we lap last year's event.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: We expect that Q4 sales growth will benefit by a similar amount for this year's event.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Overall for the enterprise, we expect sales growth in Q3 to be between 3% and 3.75%.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Regarding operating income, we're raising our full-year guidance to 7% to 8.5% versus 6% to 8% previously.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: We expect the financial impact from the tariff refund receipts and reinvestment will be largely contained within the current fiscal year, with the objective of driving sustained customer benefits and share gains in the second half and into future years.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Our guidance assumes that fuel costs persist at current rates.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: We now expect more than $2 billion of incremental fuel-related costs this year above and beyond our original guidance assumptions.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: We also expect costs related to the acquisition and integration of Vibe to be an approximate 20 basis points headwind to OI growth inclusive of planned investment of tariff refunds.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Q3 operating income growth on a constant currency basis is expected to grow 2% to 4%.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Notably, a large portion of the refunds were invested at the end of Q2, so the full-quarter impact of these investments is more pronounced in Q3.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: When looking at Q2 and Q3 reported operating income together, growth would average approximately 10% per quarter.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: We're raising our full-year EPS guidance to $2.80 to $2.87 from $2.75 to $2.85 previously.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: For Q3, we expect EPS of $0.62 to $0.64.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: I want to be really clear on this point.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: We're at the midpoint of our year, and we're raising our full-year guidance to reflect confidence in our ability to sustain growth and share gains.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Importantly, we're raising in the face of more than $2 billion of incremental cost tied to higher fuel prices in arguably a softer consumer environment than in February when we introduced our initial outlook.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: As such, we feel it's prudent to remain cautious by only raising the guide modestly.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: We now expect slightly higher capex for the year at approximately 4% of annual net sales.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Even with this increase, we expect to generate double-digit growth in free cash flow this year.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: In closing, our teams continue to focus on what we do best—serving customers and members with everyday great value, exceptional convenience and speed, all while pushing our business model forward, diversifying our profit mix, and leading in agentic experiences.

speaker: Analyst at Morgan Stanley · Simeon Gutman

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Simeon, this is John David.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Thanks for your question.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: We, no doubt, and it sort of states the obvious, have seen some incremental pressure on the consumer relative to the beginning of the year with higher fuel prices.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: As you go through month by month in the last quarter, you can tell when fuel prices increased and got above $4.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: And perhaps there's a psychological impact to that, that there are choices that consumers are making.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: So June was a little more obvious as we look at the quarter in terms of customers making trade-offs, and it's why we have leaned so heavily into lower prices.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: You're right, there is elasticity on these items that we roll out.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: We talked about 11,000 rollbacks.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: We're really proud of that and how we're trying to be there for our customers and members during this period of time.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: But I think, very importantly in your question, there is a lag to this.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: There is a bit of a cumulative benefit that comes when you lower prices.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: And so you don't necessarily expect to have that offsetting benefit to the lower prices in the immediate period.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: And so, as you know, being very familiar with our business, we're not managing our business for one quarter.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: We're managing our business on a multi-year basis to play to win.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: We feel confident in our strategy and what we're doing here.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: And importantly, the market share gains that we've seen in these recent periods, they're durable.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: We're seeing that we're keeping those market share gains, and it's why I think we've been perhaps as bold as we have to continue to go after that.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: And same with the rollbacks and the other investments.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: We exited the first quarter, as we mentioned earlier, at about 7,000 rollbacks.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: It's normally about 5.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: At the end of the quarter we had 11.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: And when you take rollbacks in consumable categories like food, you tend to see first a unit increase.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: And we saw transactions and units grow in the quarter, and then that does create a temporary deflationary effect.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: But as the units grow over time, particularly in food, then the share gains come through.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: And we were really pleased with the recent share report in food.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: It's one of the strongest reports we've had in some time.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: So we're pleased with those.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: But again, we'll handle this thoughtfully.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Our hope and intention always is that rollbacks can become permanent price decreases wherever possible.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: We have a line of sight to those, and for any that we see that we aren't getting a return on, we'll manage them carefully.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: We want to be thoughtful about how we invest all of our funds and all the funds available.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Ultimately, we're trying to reinforce the everyday low price model and save customers money.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Look, we have a lot of confidence in our ability to continue to grow the bottom line at a much faster rate than we have the top line.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: But I don't want to miss the top-line growth, too.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: To have what is roughly three-quarters of a trillion dollars of a revenue base and be able to grow at 4, 5, 6% a year, that's meaningful growth.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: And so, let's step back for a second and just think about the U.S. comp.

text: U.S. comp is at 2.5%.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: I think the right way to think about that is really more 3.5% when you adjust for health and wellness.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: But just take it at face value: at 2.5% U.S. comp, we grew operating income 10% ex-tariffs.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: That's 4x the level of revenue growth.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: We haven't done that level of profit growth relative to the U.S. comp in two decades.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Our business is fundamentally changing.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: If you look at the profit drivers of our business, almost half of the growth came from areas like membership, advertising, marketplace, and we expect this to continue.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: In fact, I think there's line of sight to seeing improvement in incremental margins as we go forward.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Right now we're generating roughly low double-digit incremental margins, but the growth drivers of our business are as intact as they ever have been.

speaker: CEO · John Furner

text: So, you know, again, like we're managing our business on an annual, if not multi-year, basis, but feel really good about what's in store for the next year and the years to come.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: But on the incremental margins, which as I noted kind of in my previous answer, I think that's a big part of the story for us.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: We continue to see these growth areas of our business that are driving more benefit to the bottom line.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: We've not really committed to any certain number around the incremental margins in our business.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: But if you look back over the last, call it six quarters or so, generally U.S. e-commerce incremental margins have been in that high single digit to low double digit range.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: A couple quarters ago, I was asked a question about the opportunity for that to improve over time, and I think I was maybe a little bit more guarded at that point.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: But when we see things like our advertising business that continues to grow at a 40% clip on a much higher base, that actually gives us confidence in the ability to maybe see incremental margins even go higher.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: And that's actually what we've been seeing, and not by a small margin, by a large margin on a larger base.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: And with the acquisition of Vibe, this gives us a new addressable market that we didn't have before in these small and medium-sized merchants.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: And so we're very excited about the opportunity there.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Advertising though is just one aspect of what we're doing.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: I don't want to solely point to that as the only opportunity that we have here.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: As we continue to add businesses that complement the diversified portfolio of offerings that we have today that generate these higher margins, it's very attractive to us.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: The key benefit of digital growth is being able to grow at a very low marginal cost.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: You know, John has talked a lot since he's come on about this platform approach that we're taking.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: We're doing all the same things that we're doing in the U.S. in our other markets around the world.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: Mexico is a really good example.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: You know, we look at Mexico today and, you know, it's the same playbook that we implemented in the U.S. five years ago.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey
text: And we're super excited about some of the early progress that we're seeing there.

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey

speaker: CFO · John David Rainey

text: Dave?
